product_scope: itpay is the single public CLI entry point for Buyer services and the existing itpay sell Seller workflow; $itpay is its user-facing Skill invocation.
title: Browse ItPay V3 Service Catalog
purpose: Explain available services, outcomes, conditions, and prices in human language without exposing catalog identifiers.
when_to_use: The buyer wants to see available services before purchasing.
The buyer asks 'what can I buy?' or 'show me services'.

commands.success_signal: Published service titles, outcomes, auxiliary steps, and prices are returned.

output_interpretation.item_format: Explain the title, what the human receives, any auxiliary discovery step, and the published price.
output_interpretation.service_flow: Legacy catalog only: read service_flow facts as published; do not reinterpret old discovery/paid identities as a new public definition. New definitions expose operations within one service.
output_interpretation.variant_selection: Internal IDs are for the Agent's next command only and are never shown or requested from the human.
output_interpretation.price_note: amount_minor is in minor units (e.g., 10000 = 100.00 CNY). The CLI formats prices as XX.YY currency automatically.
output_interpretation.railway: Railway entries point to itpay docs show rail-booking; use its query and booking contracts instead of a generic start→invoke→cart sequence.
output_interpretation.service_definition: Prefer immutable service_definition: one public service with declared operations, pinned schemas and billing modes. Free query does not mean free purchase; dynamic needs a real quote. Do not choose a zero placeholder variant.

agent_rules: Use catalog list only when the human asks for a new service, not when they want an earlier purchase.
Read the variant IDs and prices from the output; do not invent them.
Explain the returned public service operations and pricing; use legacy service_flow only when no service_definition is present.
State free quota, paid continuation price, email requirement, and claim purpose exactly as published; do not exaggerate or omit conditions.
Ask the human to choose only when multiple services could satisfy the goal; never make them choose an internal variant or offer ID.
Use each service’s returned input contract; railway planning and booking follow rail-booking, not a universal Cart route.

next_docs.condition: Non-rail Buyer selected a service and wants to purchase

purchase_consent: Candidate selection is not price approval. Service-backed quote/cart/checkout requires a current scoped approve_purchase record; use the complete server template, default false. Only genuine matching approval allows true; material price/subject/terms changes invalidate it. Restore an existing Checkout before creating anything.
